newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore tax probe began months ago - authorities.
newsitem.headline: Singapore tax probe began months ago - authorities.

text.p: An investigation into the tax affairs of a Singapore opposition politician, who is also facing defamation action from government leaders, began in the middle of last year, tax authorities said in a statement.

The monitoring of Tang Liang Hong's tax affairs dates back to "the middle of 1996, well before the general election" on January 2 this year, the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) said in a statement sent to Reuters on Thursday.
Tang's home and office were raided in the early morning hours on Tuesday by IRAS officials who seized documents they said were related to the investigation.
The IRAS said its computer system monitors the reported income of all taxpayers to detect cases with significant variations for detailed examination.

The tax investigation was made public later that day, as news broke separately that Tang had become subject to a court injunction seeking to freeze his assets or have him set aside up to US$7.9 million for possible damages and legal costs.
The request for the injunction had been filed on behalf of 11 members of Singapore's ruling People's Action Party (PAP), including Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong.
The PAP politicians had filed defamation suits against Tang for calling them liars during the election campaign.
Tang, who failed to win a hotly contested constituency in the election for the opposition Workers' Party, is in London consulting with lawyers on the case.
His wife, Teo Siew Har, is also subject of the injunction and was prevented from leaving Singapore by the Home Affairs Ministry, which has cancelled her passports.
Tang left Singapore after the election saying he had received death threats, but has said he intends to fight the lawsuits and eventually return to Singapore.
